title: Founded, Built, Established: Participles for Institutions

sections.content: The same pattern works just as well for institutions as for people. When you describe what István built — churches, monasteries, dioceses, laws — participle-titles let you name each one efficiently: *az alapított kolostor* ("the founded monastery"), *a bevezetett törvény* ("the introduced law").

items.spanish: Az alapított kolostorokban szerzetesek éltek és tanítottak.
items.english: Monks lived and taught in the founded monasteries.

items.spanish: A bevezetett törvények védték az egyház vagyonát, és büntették a pogány szokásokhoz való visszatérést.
items.english: The introduced laws protected the church's property, and punished a return to pagan customs.

items.spanish: A tíz faluban felépített templomok a keresztény rend jelei voltak.
items.english: The churches built across every ten villages were signs of the new Christian order.

sections.content: Participle-titles for institutions work exactly like the ones for people — they stay invariant, and they let you skip a whole relative clause. Compare: *a kolostor, amelyet István alapított* ("the monastery that István founded", long) vs. *az István által alapított kolostor* ("the monastery founded by István", short) — exactly the pattern you'll deepen in Lesson 5.
